transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, doctor... I came in because, since my grandson was killed, I just can't seem to feel anything good anymore. My daughter can sit right beside me, holding my hand, and I know I love her. I know it in my head. But... I just cannot feel the warmth of it inside me at all.
When exactly did your grandson pass away, and when did you start noticing this numbness and inability to feel joy?

It's been... well, it's been exactly six days. That's when he was killed outside the community center. And this numbness, this not being able to feel anything... it started right then. It's just been going on for these past six days.
Besides not feeling the warmth of your daughter's love, do you feel disconnected or detached from what's happening around you, or does it feel like things aren't quite real?

Yes, I do feel like that. It's... well, it's a bit hard to explain. But sometimes my own living room just looks flat and strange to me. It's almost like I'm looking at everything through church glass. And I feel disconnected from myself, too. It feels as if I'm just watching this old woman move around the house, instead of actually being fully in my own body.
When you say you feel like you're watching yourself move around the house, are you able to recognize that it's you, or does it feel like you're watching someone else entirely?

I know it's me. I mean, I know I'm the one walking into the kitchen or sitting in the chair. It's just... it doesn't feel like me. It feels like I'm just observing myself going through the motions, but I know it's my own body. It's just a very strange, empty feeling.

Since your grandson was killed six days ago, have you been having unwanted memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about what happened to him, or thoughts about his death that keep coming into your mind even when you don't want them to?

Yes, I have. It's... it's awful. I'll just be doing something normal, you know, like folding a quilt square or reaching for my tea, and then... all of a sudden, I hear those shots again. And I see him lying there on the ground outside the community center. It doesn't feel like a memory. It feels like it's happening right in front of me, all over again.

You mentioned these symptoms started six days ago. Have you been experiencing all of these feelings — the numbness, the disconnection from reality, the feeling of watching yourself, and the flashbacks — continuously throughout all of these six days, or have there been times when they've gotten better or gone away?
No, it hasn't really stopped or gotten better. It's been like this the whole time, for the past six days, ever since he was killed outside the community center. It's just been a constant thing.

Just to be clear about the timeline: these symptoms started exactly when your grandson was killed six days ago, correct? And before that traumatic event, you were feeling normal — no numbness, no feeling disconnected from reality, no flashbacks?

Yes, that's exactly right. I was completely normal before this happened... I didn't have any of those issues at all, no numbness or flashbacks or anything like that. It all just started right then. This has been going on for the six days since my grandson was killed outside the community center, and not a moment before.

Since your grandson was killed, have you noticed that you startle very easily — like if someone taps your shoulder or there's a sudden noise, you jump or react much more intensely than you normally would?

Yes, I have noticed that. It feels like my nerves are just completely shot. If there's a sudden noise... like when the ice maker drops cubes in the fridge, or if a car backfires down the block, my whole body jumps so hard I have to grab the table to steady myself. And my heart just keeps pounding and pounding, long after everyone else in the room has settled down. I just can't seem to help it.
You mentioned these symptoms have been going on for six days now. Do you expect they might continue, or do you think they might start to get better soon?

I honestly don't know. I mean... I would like to think they'll get better soon, but right now, it doesn't feel like it's easing up at all. I've never been through anything like this in my entire eighty-four years, so I really have no idea what to expect. I just don't know.
